meta.title: /smh-designer — Creative Vision Lock Lifecycle
meta.subtitle: How to design tactile, production-ready interfaces with 🦋 Caterpillar: Two-Phase Creative Vision Lock from prompt to implementation

views.label: Complete Vision Lock
views.note: Prompt, interview, Creative Vision Brief, vision approval STOP, implementation plan, plan approval STOP, and build execution.

views.label: The Two Approval Stops
views.note: Where Caterpillar stops for you: aesthetic alignment before architecture, and architecture approval before code.

views.label: Creative Craft Engines
views.note: Grounding in the 7 craft engines: design systems, Apple springs, shaders, glass, 3D scenes, mobile motion, and border beams.

nodes.label: Launch Intent
nodes.description: Invoke /smh-designer with natural language intent (e.g. 'frosted glass pricing card with sunset border beam') or explore the 10-category interactive capabilities menu.
details: Direct Intent Dispatch: Prompts with arguments skip menus and immediately begin Phase 1 Creative Discovery.

Capabilities Menu: Interactive menu covering [BS] Brainstorm, [DS] Design Systems, [FM] Fluid Motion, [WG] WebGPU Shaders, [LG] Apple Glass, [3D] Spatial UI, [BB] Border Beam & Glows, [AV] Alpha Video, [AU] Design Audit, [CD] Scaffold.
Express Lane: Trivial single-line styling tweaks skip the ceremony and make the fix directly.

nodes.label: Creative Discovery
nodes.description: Caterpillar interviews you on visual emotion, tactile materials, and interaction momentum before writing any code or architecture.
details: Shared Vocabulary: Fills the five request slots — WHERE (viewport/state), WHAT (screen/component), WHICH LAYER (stroke/glow/bloom), WHICH KNOB (reach/speed/strength), HOW MUCH.
Tactile Grounding: Pins down whether surfaces need Apple frosted glass, live DOM liquid glass refraction, WebGPU plasma backdrops, or optical border glows.
Non-Negotiable Invariants: Mobile-first viewport baseline, sub-300ms UI animation budget, never ease-in, never animate from scale(0).

nodes.label: Vision Brief
nodes.description: Synthesizes discovery into a formal Creative Vision Brief specifying palettes, typography, motion curves, and optical materials.
details: Design Tokens: Curated color palette (e.g. Ocean, Sunset, Obsidian), typography hierarchy, and spacing tokens via ui-ux-pro-max.
Spring Physics: Precise Apple 2-parameter spring curves (e.g. 0.35s critically damped) and tactile micro-interaction press feedback.
Shaders & FX: Verified shader parameters, border beam travel presets, and 2D canvas AI Thinking Indicators.

nodes.label: ⛔ Stop 1: Vision Gate
nodes.description: First mandatory approval stop. Caterpillar halts execution until you review the brief and confirm: 'Approved'.
details: Zero Blind Coding: Guarantees no agent spends tokens building an interface whose look and feel was never agreed.
Strict Gate Trigger: Refuses vague affirmations like 'looks good' or 'continue' — requires explicit approval.
Iterative Refinement: Easy to adjust mood, speed, or materials in conversation before architecture begins.

nodes.label: Technical Plan
nodes.description: Translates the approved visual direction into an engineering-grade implementation plan with component breakdown and performance constraints.
details: Component Architecture: TSX component decomposition, clean prop interfaces, and state boundaries.
Hardware-Composited Rules: GPU acceleration (transform and opacity only), sub-pixel mask composites, and ~30fps rAF pulse driver.
Dual-Viewport QA Plan: Test specifications measuring layout and visual correctness at both phone (375x667) and desktop viewports.

nodes.label: ⛔ Stop 2: Plan Gate
nodes.description: Second mandatory approval stop. The operator reviews the technical implementation plan, prop contracts, and test criteria.
details: Final Checkpoint: Validates bundle size limits, mobile battery constraints, and component layout before code generation.
Command Boundary: This is where /smh-designer deliberately finishes — it delivers an agreed plan, ready for execution.
Full Operator Control: No surprises, regressions, or uncontrolled dependency sprawl.

nodes.label: Build & Verify
nodes.description: Hand off the approved plan directly to your coding agent or build lane (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, or manual implementation).
details: Straight to Build: The implementation plan's verification section is structured to be executable as-is.
Ticket-First Option: Mint a tracking item (Jira, GitHub Issues, Linear) from the acceptance criteria if desired.
Production Delivery: Component implementation, responsive testing, and final visual polish review.
